body:
SECOND CORRECTION -- WARRANT#491. THE CAPACITY NUMBER WAS AN 11x UNDERSTATEMENT.

Manuel pushed back: "i doubt your compounding is actually compounding, things go from 31 dollars to
500k etc so why would it slow in millions". He was right, and this supersedes the ceiling figures
in BOTH previous messages.

WHAT WAS NEVER WRONG: the compounding does not slow. 18.0x/yr held the whole way -- $100 -> $1.78k
-> $31.8k -> $571k -> $9.16M, the same multiple every year, no decay. What throttled was the EDGE,
through ONE guessed input: CAPACITY_NOTIONAL = $25M, the position size at which fills were assumed
to degrade. I flagged it as the weakest number in the chain and then let every headline rest on it.

DERIVED PROPERLY. Market impact follows the SQUARE-ROOT LAW: impact = sigma * sqrt(Q/V), so
Q = V * (tolerated_impact/sigma)^2. Every term is measurable -- sigma is the ATR already used
throughout (1.80 bp/bar), V is public FX spot turnover, and the entry can be worked over 30 minutes
since the median hold is 4.8 hours. Tolerance set at 25% of the 2.0 bp top-band edge.

  pair       spot $/day     capacity/position
  EURUSD       $400B              $643.00M
  USDJPY       $250B              $401.88M
  GBPUSD       $110B              $176.83M
  USDCHF        $55B               $88.41M
  EURJPY        $35B               $56.26M
  MEAN                            $273.28M       <- vs my $25M guess. LOW BY 11x.

Even the THINNEST of the five absorbs twice what I had assumed for all of them.

EVERYTHING THAT CHANGES:
                                OLD ($25M guess)        DERIVED ($273M)
  erosion begins                       $6.32M                 $69.08M
  E*, operate here                     $8.01M                 $87.56M
  wall, growth zero                   $12.54M                $137.08M
  income at E*                     $19.55M/yr             $213.70M/yr
  instruments for $1B                     624                      57

ON FIVE MARKETS ALONE, NO WIDTH ADDED: the account compounds at the full unbroken 18x/yr all the
way to $87.56M, which is 4.7 years from $100. That is the direct answer to Manuel's challenge.

THE TOLERANCE IS A CHOICE, NOT A FACT -- the whole curve, so it is visible:
  10% of edge (0.20 bp)  -> capacity  $43.72M, E*  $14.01M, wall  $21.93M
  25% of edge (0.50 bp)  -> capacity $273.28M, E*  $87.56M, wall $137.08M   <- used
  50% of edge (1.00 bp)  -> capacity   $1.09B, E* $350.23M, wall $548.30M
  100% of edge (2.00 bp) -> capacity   $4.37B, E*   $1.40B, wall   $2.19B

STILL TRUE: capacity is real and finite. Impact rises as sqrt(size) -- it can be outrun a long way
but never escaped. The ceiling moved 11x; it did not vanish. Volumes are BIS survey reads taken
deliberately on the low side.

THE RISK HAS CHANGED CATEGORY. At $87M running 152 trades/day, LIQUIDITY is not what stops this --
THE BROKER is. A retail counterparty that B-books the flow stops quoting a consistently profitable
account long before any interbank limit is reached. That is a commercial decision, no volume figure
predicts it, and it is now the most likely thing to end the run early. Two questions for them:
  1. LEVERAGE TIER by account equity (the 80-concurrent book needs 110:1 gross) -- still unanswered
  2. B-book / market maker, or true STP/ECN?

SUPERSESSION TRAIL, so nothing stale gets acted on:
  #488 said $1B in ~51 years  -- WRONG FRAMING (fixed 5-market book harvesting to cash)
  #490 corrected the framing  -- right shape, but built on the $25M guess
  #491 (this) corrects the capacity number -- 11x higher, so #490's tables are conservative by
       roughly that factor and its "instruments needed" column drops from 624 to 57.
